name: Balanced Removals (Harder)
description: This is a harder version of the problem. In this version, $$$n \le 50\,000$$$. There are $$$n$$$ distinct points in three-dimensional space numbered from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$. The $$$i$$$-th point has coordinates $$$(x_i, y_i, z_i)$$$. The number of points $$$n$$$ is even. You'd like to remove all $$$n$$$ points using a sequence of $$$\frac{n}{2}$$$ snaps. In one snap, you can remove any two points $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$ that have not been removed yet and form a perfectly balanced pair. A pair of points $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$ is perfectly balanced if no other point $$$c$$$ (that has not been removed yet) lies within the axis-aligned minimum bounding box of points $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$. Formally, point $$$c$$$ lies within the axis-aligned minimum bounding box of points $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$ if and only if $$$\min(x_a, x_b) \le x_c \le \max(x_a, x_b)$$$, $$$\min(y_a, y_b) \le y_c \le \max(y_a, y_b)$$$, and $$$\min(z_a, z_b) \le z_c \le \max(z_a, z_b)$$$. Note that the bounding box might be degenerate. Find a way to remove all points in $$$\frac{n}{2}$$$ snaps.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 50\,000$$$; $$$n$$$ is even), denoting the number of points. Each of the next $$$n$$$ lines contains three integers $$$x_i$$$, $$$y_i$$$, $$$z_i$$$ ($$$-10^8 \le x_i, y_i, z_i \le 10^8$$$), denoting the coordinates of the $$$i$$$-th point. No two points coincide.
output_specification: Output $$$\frac{n}{2}$$$ pairs of integers $$$a_i, b_i$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i, b_i \le n$$$), denoting the indices of points removed on snap $$$i$$$. Every integer between $$$1$$$ and $$$n$$$, inclusive, must appear in your output exactly once. We can show that it is always possible to remove all points. If there are many solutions, output any of them.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1237C2 — Balanced Removals (Harder) [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
